record.summary: Non-binding Commission guidelines, issued under Article 96(1)(d) of the AI Act, on the transparency obligations of Article 50, which apply from 2 August 2026. They explain who must comply and how: informing people that they are interacting with an AI system, machine-readable marking and detection of AI-generated or manipulated content, informing people exposed to emotion recognition or biometric categorisation, and labelling deep fakes and AI-generated text on matters of public interest. They cover exceptions, the horizontal requirements of Article 50(5) on clear, timely and accessible information, and enforcement.
record.notes: The guidelines are the annex to a Communication to the Commission approving their content, C(2026) 5054 final of 20 July 2026. Their drafting drew on a broad consultation, input from the Member States in the AI Board and comments on draft guidelines published for consultation on 8 May 2026. They complement the Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content (EU-16): providers and deployers may rely on a code assessed as adequate to demonstrate compliance. Under the AI Omnibus (EU-18), providers of generative AI systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 have until 2 December 2026 to meet the Article 50(2) marking obligation, while the disclosure obligation for interactive systems applies from 2 August 2026; content generated before 2 August 2026 need not be marked or labelled retroactively. The Commission will review the guidelines as necessary and may withdraw or amend them.

title.quote: 1 - Guidelines on the implementation of the transparency obligations for certain AI systems under Article 50 of the AI Act
Guidelines on the implementation of the transparency obligations for certain AI systems under Article 50 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the 'AI Act')
Commission publishes guidelines on transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems

status.quote: The Commission adopted these guidelines to offer practical guidance to competent authorities, as well as providers and deployers of AI systems.

The European Commission has published guidelines to assist providers and deployers of artificial intelligence (AI) systems in meeting the AI Act's transparency obligations, which start to apply on 2 August 2026.
These Guidelines are non -binding. Any authoritative interpretation of the AI Act may ultimately only be given by the Court of Justice of the European Union

The European Commission has published guidelines
Pursuant to Article 96(1)(d) AI Act, these Commission Guidelines are issued with the aim to serve as practical guidance

summary.quote: These transparency obligations apply two years after the entry into force of the AI Act, i.e. as from 2 August 2026.

Under the AI Act, AI providers will have to design AI systems to inform users when they are directly interacting with an AI and they will have to add machine-readable marks to enable the detection of AI-generated or manipulated content.

Deployers will also have to inform people when they are exposed to deep fakes, to AI-generated content on matters of public interests without human review or editorial control, and to emotion recognition or biometric categorisation systems.
